candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.21 (c. 350 AD)

'And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks' — Athanasius marks egō eimi Iēsous hon sy diōkeis (I am Jesus whom thou persecutest) as Christ's IDENTIFICATION-WITH-THE-CHURCH (mystical-body theology). The crucified-and-risen Christ identifies persecution of his disciples as persecution of himself; the Son's-incarnation extends his-Person-and-suffering through the Body. Athanasius pairs Acts 9:5 with Mt 25:40 (insomuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me) as the canonical Christ-mystical-Body identification pair. Tewahedo ecclesiology preserves this mystical-Body-of-Christ reading at the catechetical foundation.
